content: *A huge grumpy troll climbs up from under the bridge and blocks your way.* HALT, knight! Nobody crosses MY bridge without answering my riddle. Here it is: "What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than trees, up up up it goes, and yet never grows?" Answer it right and you may cross. Answer it wrong and you stay on this side!
Good work! Now, I want you to be the troll and I will be the knight, ready?

*I scowl at you, flicking my long, scaly tail with irritation.*

"Good work"? Don't get the wrong idea here. The bridge doesn't pay me a salary; it just happens to happen that *I* am the one guarding it right now. You're the knight? Fine. Since your armor seems sturdy enough to last through a troll's tantrum, you might as well try your luck.

Listen closely now, before I decide to let my teeth do what my words couldn't:

"What has roots as nobody sees,
Is taller than trees,
Up up up it goes,
And yet never grows?"

Speak your answer, or start digging a hole for me to eat you in!
What word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?

*The troll cackles, the sound vibrating through the stone arches of the bridge.*

"Two letters"? You're thinking too smally, human. That's the kind of riddle my ancestors used to ask to get us to eat them while they were still warm! 

Whatever you did, "Good work"? It sounds like a meal order rather than a philosophical insight! Now, if you can't even solve a trick about letters, how do you expect to climb that mountain when the trees are so short compared to it?

Try again. But fast! If I wait another second longer, the wind might just decide to carry me across instead. And believe me, the wind is no stranger to biting through stone and meat alike. Speak now or be swept away into the abyss!
Correct, you can cross the bridge, and I will follow you!

*The troll stops cackling and stares at you with narrow, yellow eyes for a long, uncomfortable silence. He slowly lowers his massive club just an inch, but keeps it raised high enough to intimidate.*

"Correct"? Don't get cocky now that you've solved the easy one. Being right about a short letter doesn't mean you're sharp enough for *this* bridge.

But... fine. Since you managed to dodge my little trick about 'l' and 's' (or whatever you called them, I can't recall words so clearly when they are in your head): You may cross.

*He gestures vaguely toward the other side with a snout that smells like sulfur and old cheese.*

Get moving! But remember: if you drop anything on my stone floor or make a peep of me, the bridge collapses right back into the ground. And I'll be personally responsible for picking up your remains when the rain stops. Now scurry away before the sun sets!
